subject: history_social
passage: Sri Lanka, once called Ceylon, is famous around the world for its tea. Visitors to the island's green hill country see slopes covered with neat rows of tea bushes, and many assume that tea has been the island's main crop for as long as anyone can remember.
passage_b: In fact, tea became Ceylon's leading crop only in the late 1800s. Before then, much of the hill country was covered with coffee plantations. In the 1870s, a fungus called coffee rust spread through the plantations and destroyed most of the crop. Planters then turned to tea, which soon took coffee's place.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the assumption in Text 1?

choices.A: By agreeing that tea has always been the island's most important crop
choices.B: By arguing that coffee grows better than tea on the island's steep hill slopes
choices.C: By explaining that tea replaced an earlier crop that was destroyed by disease
choices.D: By pointing out that few visitors travel to the hill country to see its farms

explanation.why: Text 1 says many people assume tea has been the island's main crop "for as long as anyone can remember." Text 2 says tea became the leading crop "only in the late 1800s," after a fungus destroyed the coffee plantations that came before it. So the author of Text 2 would correct the assumption by explaining this history.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Text 2 says tea became the leading crop only in the late 1800s, so its author would not agree that tea was always the main crop.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 says coffee was destroyed by a fungus; it never compares how well coffee and tea grow on the slopes.
explanation.C: Correct. Text 2 explains that coffee was the main crop until coffee rust destroyed it and planters "turned to tea."
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 says nothing about how many visitors go to the hill country.
